reviewer: Claude Opus (fresh, non-author, independent specification reviewer; review04)
verdict: APPROVED — task 1.1a specification scope only. No blocking findings. Findings F1–F7 are binding readings and constraints on the implementation and its tests. F8 is a later obligation.
task1_1aMayBegin: YES, conditionally. Grok may begin the 1.1a production repair only when all of these hold: (1) fresh Astra medium also approves the same candidateSha256 with an identical 1.1a scope; (2) the RED tests from the prior tests-only 1.1 approval exist and fail against current policy.py/store.py/cli.py through the actual caller path (see F3); (3) the canonical-store inventory stays retained as the pre-source anchor record. If Astra is unavailable, blocks, or approves a different scope, or if the relevant specification bytes change, 1.1a does not begin.
approvedItems: 1.4 — only the isolated policy/store/history/CLI checks corresponding to 1.1a
approvedScope: Specification approval for these exact package bytes. Covered: a source repair in existing plugins/moriarty-dev/scripts/moriarty_dev/policy.py, store.py and their cli.py callers (cmd_status, cmd_next, cmd_run including the post-reservation recheck, cmd_review, history_reader construction), plus isolated tests. The repair makes every action with evidenceProfile exactly 'finalized-financial-settlement' obey the operational-history, repeated-failure and primary gates regardless of kind. Such actions also occupy the primary slot in store.reserve's transactional check, get_history primaryActive and has_other_primary, in both start orderings. Live-profile history comes only from a canonical store with a positively matched persisted identity; otherwise it is unavailable, never zero failures. That makes it unavailable for the actual canonical store today, which has no identity. Approval ingestion clears only findings it explicitly resolves. Tests run only on copied or temporary SQLite stores and locks with explicit destinations. Live-store digests and counts, including WAL/SHM sidecars, must be unchanged across the test interval. Excluded, not waived: records.py live labels and SP01 bridge (1.2); closed label strings other than the fixed discriminator; runner, ledger producer, budget.lock, master claim and store-token/master binding (1.3); resource amendment or grant; creating, bootstrapping or adopting a persisted identity in the live store; live history reconciliation; attempt-count derivation; non-mutating wallet observations; action registration; live accounting mutation; debit; dispatch; items 2–6. This approval grants no source acceptance, which still needs both fresh source audits of the frozen 1.1a candidate. It grants no live admission, resource authority or actual-result acceptance. All later product acceptance obligations, including original MC02 predicates, I2 uncertified until MC05 and SP05's SP01 dependency, remain in force.

findings.class: canonical-history selection / no live identity creation
findings.path: spec.md#Item 1 — Operational history is evidence; store.py::SCHEMA_SQL, init_db, get_db_path, get_history; cli.py (history_reader construction, bootstrap_store import)
findings.requirement: Fail-closed must be a positive identity match, not detection of an override. A temporary git-layout copy reached through default get_db_path resolution holds no override flag and would pass an override-only check. init_db runs SCHEMA_SQL on every write-path call, including live status record_admin_interval and review. An identity table or token added to SCHEMA_SQL or bootstrap_store would therefore be created in the live store on the next guarded call. That is excluded live identity creation.
findings.correction: Implement live-profile history as available only when a persisted in-store token matches an explicitly supplied anchor. In 1.1a, no production CLI flag, environment variable, file or records path may supply that anchor. Fixture anchoring is only an in-process argument in tests. Reading identity must tolerate its absence without writing schema or tokens. Tests must show unavailable history for all of: the actual inventoried schema with no token (copy); a fresh store; an unrelated-event-seeded store; an explicit --db or override destination; a temporary clone resolved by default. Tests must also show no identity table or row appears after exercising status/review/run on a copied pre-existing-schema store.

findings.path: store.py::reservations schema, reserve, get_history primary_active query; cli.py::has_other_primary (not supplied)
findings.requirement: Reservation rows record action_kind but no evidence profile. Occupancy by live verify/review/reproduce needs a determinable profile. An ALTER/column migration in init_db would change live schema at next use, which the 1.1a text does not authorize.
findings.correction: Prefer deriving profile from existing transactional data written in the same reserve transaction. If a schema change is unavoidable, disclose it explicitly in the source-review packet and test it against a copied pre-existing-schema store. Any active reservation whose profile cannot be determined occupies the slot (fail closed). The inventoried live store has no active reservations, so this has no present effect. Test both orderings three ways: via reserve's IMMEDIATE-transaction conflict, via get_history primaryActive, and via has_other_primary after reservation. Include a genuine concurrent-start case on a copied store.

findings.severity: non-blocking for 1.1a (fail-closed); blocking for later identity adoption
findings.class: lineage repository-key divergence / vacuous RED risk
findings.path: store.py::reserve, finish, record_event, record_review (repository=str(repo)); store.py::_canonical_repo_ids, get_history; records.py docstring ('repository is the resolved git-common-dir'); canonical-store-before-source.json
findings.requirement: Writers key events by the checkout path passed in. The inventory shows linked-worktree paths, e.g. SP01.6 events under .worktrees/moriarty-dev-plugin-grok. get_history matches only ids derived from the queried value, and the reader contract says that value is the git common dir. Linked worktrees sharing one store therefore cannot see each other's lineage events. Today, a worktree with any admin_cycle event passes total_events>0 and reads zero failures; afk-live-financial-execution has one. Revision 4's identity rule prevents this from granting live history now. However, a RED test that calls get_history with hand-matched repository strings may pass or fail for reasons the real caller never exhibits.
findings.correction: (a) Drive at least the seeded-store, renamed-lineage and approval-ingestion RED/GREEN cases through the actual cli → load_snapshot → history_reader keying. Where that path already yields unavailable because of key mismatch, record the observation rather than crediting the repair. (b) In anchored fixture simulation, treat repository-key variance among linked worktrees of one common dir as a lineage rename: counted or unavailable, never zero. (c) Before any later identity adoption or history reconciliation, resolve the keying explicitly.

findings.class: repeated-failure gate outcome for live non-repair kinds
findings.path: spec.md#Scenario: Live kind, lineage or approval cannot shed history; policy.py::RETRY_BLOCKED_KINDS, repair readiness branch
findings.requirement: The scenario fixes denial without verified reproduction and changed approach. It defines the gate as 'the same gates as the corresponding live implementation'. Current implement semantics deny at ≥2 regardless of readiness.
findings.correction: Tests assert the literal reading. A live-profile verify/review/reproduce/admin action with sameDefectFailures ≥ 2 is denied regardless of reproducerVerified/approachChanged. Live repair keeps the existing readiness rule. Reproduction proceeds through non-live-profile actions. Allowing live non-repair kinds on readiness would require a specification revision.

findings.path: spec.md ('regardless of kind', 'both obey and occupy the primary slot regardless of kind'); policy.py report early-return, HISTORY_EXEMPT_KINDS, docstring; cli.py::cmd_run report path
findings.requirement: 'Regardless of kind' covers report and admin. A live-profile report currently bypasses every gate. Its reservation writes action_start/action_end events into the lineage, which is the seeding pattern the spec forbids.
findings.correction: For evidenceProfile exactly 'finalized-financial-settlement', the unconditional report allowance and the history exemptions do not apply. Both report and admin obey and occupy the slot. Non-live report and verify/review/reproduce semantics stay unchanged, and docstrings are updated. No current catalog action uses that profile, so present behavior is unaffected. Keeping live report always allowed would be a specification change.

findings.path: store.py::get_history result_review branch (unresolved_findings.clear()), record_review event_kind labeling; cli.py::cmd_review target-action inference
findings.requirement: No closed discriminator separates specification/source/resource receipts from actual-result receipts before item 1.2's closed labels. The only deterministic 1.1a guard is on the clearing effect itself.
findings.correction: An APPROVED receipt removes only findings explicitly listed in resolvedFindings/resolved, within the same lineage. It never clears all findings. Apply this universally. Clear-all launders any lineage, and the canonical SP01.6 lineage has no findings, so there is no observable historical regression. Do not claim that 1.1a relabels non-result approvals; that awaits 1.2 labels. Preserve the existing behavior that non-APPROVED receipts create defect_failure rows; it is fail-closed. Tests: an approval without a list leaves all findings; an approval naming X in another lineage leaves X; an approval naming X in this lineage removes only X.

findings.path: spec.md#Guarded status... paragraph; tasks.md#1.1a/1.4; store.py::init_db (WAL), get_history (default-mode connect), get_db_path
findings.requirement: The live store runs in WAL mode. Hashing only state.sqlite3 can miss writes, and a default-mode connect can create sidecars or checkpoint. get_db_path resolves any linked worktree, including the implementation worktree, to the live common-dir store. Concurrent orchestrator status calls may write admin_intervals during the test interval.
findings.correction: Record digests, sizes and row counts of state.sqlite3 plus any -wal/-shm before and after the test interval. Inspect with mode=ro or immutable=1 URIs. Run every test CLI invocation with an explicit isolated destination, and assert before any write that the resolved path is outside the live common dir. Attribute any concurrent permitted admin_intervals writes separately with process and time; do not waive a digest change.

findings.path: proposal.md revision-4 inventory paragraph; references/execution-focus.md (collector author attempts, executor06); deliverables/sp05-financial-integration-2026-09-09/preview-loan-exit-01/

findings.requirement: Disposition of each predecessor finding against revision 4.
findings.correction: N1 addressed: canonical store only, identity absence recorded, override refusal, seeded/other-clone/restored scenario, lineage inventory; see F1 and F3 for mechanism constraints. limitations: No tools were run against repository bytes. The candidateSha256 and per-file digests were not recomputed; the review relies on the supplied inline bytes and manifest.

policy.py and runner.py were supplied whole. records.py, store.py and cli.py were selected excerpts. Not inspected: load_snapshot, read_actions, has_other_primary, record_admin_interval, bootstrap_store, CLI argument parsing and any existing db-destination override, and notifications.py. F2, F3 and F5 infer caller behavior from the excerpts and the records.py docstring.
The predecessor opus-verdict.json was supplied inline but is not in the hashed file manifest. It was used as historical context only.
The canonical-store inventory is an aggregated JSON of counts. Event IDs 3–6 come from proposal prose, not from a retained per-row extract.

This approval does not cover: 1.2, 1.3, 1.5; the remaining 1.4 producer, race, crash and attempt checks; the SP01 exact-diff disposition; the conditional successor-grant option; identity adoption; live history reconciliation; any live mutation or dispatch; items 2–6. Missing later live-instance evidence keeps live admission unavailable.

This verdict is one of two required votes. It authorizes 1.1a only together with a matching fresh Astra medium approval of the same bytes and scope. Changed relevant specification bytes require fresh approvals from both reviewers.
